memory_update.text: POWL is a useful reference anchor for medium-voltage switchgear and electrical distribution bottlenecks, but its June 2026 market cap above $10B and increasing attention make it less suitable for the underfollowed lane.

WLDN is a low-attention services candidate for policy-to-project conversion: utility programs, government infrastructure, grid modernization, energy consulting, and possible permitting/interconnection adjacency.
MYRG maps directly to power-delivery field execution: transmission, distribution, substations, commercial/industrial electrical work, and data-center electrical demand.

AMRC is a small-cap distributed-energy and government/federal infrastructure candidate whose relevance increases if data centers and public agencies use microgrids or onsite power to bypass grid constraints.

Further Layer 1B passes should search for US-listed transformer component suppliers, relay/protection/testing vendors, NETA electrical testing firms, environmental permitting consultants, and privately held bottlenecks with public parents.

node: Grid, power-equipment, and permitting execution bottlenecks
summary: Expanded the node through the underfollowed lane. The strongest discovered exposures are not utilities or hyperscalers but specialty electrical constructors, power-delivery contractors, grid/data-center energy consultants, and medium-voltage electrical equipment suppliers that convert policy-supported electrification, data-center load growth, utility capex, and government/federal energy projects into executable infrastructure. POWL is included as a reference/pure-play electrical-equipment anchor despite crossing the preferred market-cap range. WLDN, MYRG, and AMRC remain the cleaner underfollowed lane for services, engineering, program implementation, microgrids, and customer-side energy infrastructure.
